## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important item needs fixing: `--exclude` has no `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment default, which breaks the project's CLI-flag rule. The filtering logic and its tests had no defects in the reviewed scope.

## Changes
This PR adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect()` uses it with `fnmatch` to skip any file whose base name matches a pattern and logs each skipped path. The PR also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log`, the flag ignores it and still defaults to `[]`, because `default=[]` never reads the environment. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, so unwanted files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, split on a documented separator such as `os.pathsep` or a comma, then add the variable to the `docs/flags.md` row and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
